voice-statement-no-interpretation.notes: The italic Proposition (lines 1-30) is the bare Alt-isotype identification; the 'purely algebraic, no archimedean' note (lines 32-36) is a scope clarification, not physical interpretation injected into the claim.

fit-section-chapter.notes: Baryon-integrand isotype identification is on-scope for the baryon/Galois section; the ts chapter:'archimedean-universe' tag is the Phase-5 split residue, not a topical misplacement.

wall-side-statement.evidence: baryon-product-from-alt.md:32: "This is a purely algebraic statement: it lives over the categorical base ring $R$ and makes no use of the archimedean fibre functor $\tau$" vs baryon-product-from-alt.lean:79: "theorem baryonProductFromAlt (a b c : ℝ)"
wall-side-statement.notes: The .md emphatically declares the statement purely algebraic over generic R with no archimedean content, yet the .lean specialises the Vandermonde identity to (a b c : ℝ). Per §7c the `ring` identity holds over any CommRing, so the ℝ specialisation is gratuitous; should be generic R. Minor wall-side leak.

wall-side-proof.notes: No narrative `**Proof.**` body in this proposition block (the proof lives in baryon-product-from-alt-proof).

proof-narrative-lean-equiv.evidence: baryon-product-from-alt.lean:79-82: theorem proves the Vandermonde cofactor = (b-a)(c-a)(c-b) by `ring`
proof-narrative-lean-equiv.notes: The .md Proposition asserts the integrand ∏dc_k/dz is the Alt^3-isotype projection of the S_3-module (an isotype-decomposition claim). The .lean proves only the 3x3 Vandermonde determinant factorization underlying it -- a true sub-lemma, but materially narrower than the stated proposition; the isotype-projection content is not formalised.

proof-statement-integrity.notes: No weakening-to-pass or axiom injection; the Lean theorem is an honest determinantal identity with a docstring openly stating it is the 'determinantal form', ts validation:not_checked.

proof-no-self-assuming-projection.notes: baryonProductFromAlt is proved by `ring`, not by projecting a structure field equal to the conclusion.

proof-no-trivial-true.notes: The Vandermonde cofactor=discriminant identity is a genuine non-trivial polynomial identity, not a tautology; the helper sign-character lemmas are also substantive.

proof-no-false-premise.notes: No false premise; the identity holds for all a,b,c.

proof-no-unused-hypotheses.notes: baryonProductFromAlt has only the variables a,b,c (all used); no spurious hypotheses.

da-false-claim.notes: Alt^3 isotype = sign-projection, the R[S_3]=R⊕R⊕R^{2x2} Wedderburn decomposition, and the Vandermonde^2=discriminant are correct; the integrand assignment to the sign block is right.

da-vacuous.notes: Substantive proposition; the .lean proves a real (if narrower) determinantal identity, not a `: True` vacuity.

da-circular.notes: Isotype selection forced by quark color content / Wedderburn decomposition; not back-fitted.

da-overclaim.evidence: baryon-product-from-alt.md:1: "**Proposition (Alt-isotype identification...)**" with .lean proving only the Vandermonde factorization
da-overclaim.notes: The proposition-kind statement asserts the full isotype identification, but the formal backing covers only the determinantal sub-identity; the proven content is narrower than the proposition's stated scope (mild overclaim of formalisation status, ts validation:not_checked mitigates).

da-hidden-dof.notes: No free parameter; sign-isotype fixed by group theory.

da-non-sequitur.notes: The sum=trivial-isotype / product=sign-isotype / standard-isotype assignment is consistent with the S_3 representation theory; no broken inference.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.evidence: baryon-product-from-alt.lean:60-82: docstring 'The S_3-sign-isotype projection ... is the cofactor expansion of the 3x3 Vandermonde', theorem proves only that factorization
da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: The Lean proves a vacuously-narrower statement (Vandermonde factorization) than the .md isotype-projection proposition; honest partial formalisation flagged by the docstring, not a divergence to triviality -- minor.

da-citation-misuse.notes: fulton1991 (Frobenius character / sign-isotype projection) and macdonald1995 (Vandermonde discriminant) are correctly attributed.

da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: Color-tube cubic F, roots c_k(z), S_3 action, the three isotypes, and lambda_baryon all defined; the generic base ring R is named (the only slip is the .lean's ℝ specialisation).

da-empirical-fragility.notes: No numerical observable match; purely algebraic isotype claim.

da-physical-implausibility.notes: Antisymmetric color-singlet (Alt^3) for the baryon matches QCD color structure.

da-reproducibility.notes: The .lean §Witness cites computations/baryon-product-from-alt.witness.json as a 'pointwise + thimble-period numerical certificate', but no such witness file exists anywhere under computations/ (verified by find). The cited certificate is missing/irreproducible.

da-referee-verdict.evidence: baryon-product-from-alt.lean:26 missing witness + lean.ref specialised to ℝ for a claimed-generic-R statement
da-referee-verdict.notes: The proposition is mathematically correct. Strongest objections: (1) the cited numerical witness file does not exist; (2) the .lean formalises only the Vandermonde sub-identity (over ℝ) while the proposition claims a generic-R isotype projection -- so the formal backing is both narrower and gratuitously archimedean.
